title: Ham, sliced, pre-packaged, deli meat (96% fat free, water added)

content.title: About
content.content: Sliced ham is a ready‑to‑eat deli meat product made from lean pork cuts that are cooked, smoked, and then thinly sliced. The label indicates 96 % fat free with added water to retain juiciness and improve texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ham is a classic ingredient in sandwiches, salads, and snack platters.
Many flavor variations exist: classic, herb‑seasoned, smoked, mustard‑glazed, etc.
It is typically sold in thin slices, making it easy to layer or dice.
Water addition allows lower fat content without sacrificing mouthfeel.
Packaging is usually vacuum‑sealed, extending shelf life.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Ham provides complete animal protein essential for muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: With 96 % fat‑free content, it fits well into low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc, and phosphorus important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: Ready‑to‑eat format saves time on meal preparation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham often contains high levels of salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Nitrites and other preservatives may be used to extend shelf life.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to pork.

items.title: Storage safety
items.content: Although ready‑to‑eat, it should be kept at proper refrigeration temperatures to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ham can be eaten straight from the package, added to sandwiches, salads, wraps, or used in hot dishes such as omelets, pasta, and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. If frozen, it can be kept for up to 2 months.
